predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: the satrapy of Bactria: the kingdom 'was founded by the Seleucid satrap Diodotus I Soter in about 256 BC'

successors.name: Yuezhi
successors.text: Bactria, which the Yuezhi invaded 'from 130 BC' and held to c.

successors.name: Indo-Greek Kingdom
successors.text: the land south of the Hindu Kush: Heliocles 'abandoned Bactria and moved his capital to the Kabul valley'

ledger.x: 256 BC: Diodotus I Soter, the Seleucid satrap, founds the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom in Bactria.
224 BC: Euthydemus I overthrows Diodotus II and starts a new dynasty.
203: the kingdom grows north into Sogdia and Ferghana.

c. 190 BC: Demetrius I invades north-west India. 'Demetrius started the invasion of northwestern India between 190 and 180 BC', after 'the destruction of the Mauryan dynasty by the general Pushyamitra Shunga'. The earliest year of the page's range.

c. 180 BC: Demetrius I annexes the Kabul valley, Sindh and part of the Punjab. 'He annexed the Kabul valley, Sindh and a part of Punjab' (note); the invasion began 'before 180 BC'. The main page says it 'was completed by 175 BC, creating the Indo-Greek Kingdom'. The land is read as Mauryan remnant (Shunga held the…

c. 171 BC: Eucratides seizes power in Bactria. 'seems to have seized power through a coup around 171 BC'; infobox reign 171-145; the Eucratides page names Antimachus I as the probable king he dethroned. The Euthydemid line ends; same state.
c. 170 BC: Mithridates I of Parthia takes Margiana. 'Having taken Tapuria and Margiana from Demetrius in about 170 BC, Mithridates I attempted to conquer Bactria but was checked by Eucratides.'
158 BC: Aria and Margiana are lost to the Parthians.
158 BC: the fighting with Parthia ends at the end of the page's 162-158 span.
144: Sogdia and Fergana pass to the Yuezhi.
130 BC: Heliocles leaves Bactria for the Kabul valley.
127 BC: the Greek kingdom of Bactria is over.

wars.name: Siege of Bactra (Antiochus III's campaign)
wars.outcome: Euthydemus lost the battle on the Arius, then resisted a three-year siege of Bactra; Antiochus recognised his rule and promised a daughter to Demetrius (c.

wars.name: Demetrius I's invasion of India
wars.outcome: Demetrius annexed the Kabul valley, Sindh and part of the Punjab; 'completed by 175 BC' on the main page, which names the result the Indo-Greek Kingdom.

wars.name: Eucratides' wars with the Indo-Greek kings
wars.outcome: Eucratides 'conquered parts of India' as far as Barigaza and was 'besieged by Demetrius, king of the Indians', whom the page identifies uncertainly (Demetrius I, Demetrius II or Menander I); killed returning from India c.

wars.name: Parthian conquest of Aria and Margiana
wars.outcome: Mithridates I took Margiana (about 170), then 'From 162-158 BCE' Aria and Margiana, but was 'checked by Eucratides' in Bactria; the main page adds an alliance with the Seleucid Demetrius II against Parthia in 141.

wars.name: Yuezhi and Saka invasions of Bactria
wars.outcome: Heliocles, 'considered the last Greek king to reign over the Bactrian country', lost Bactria to the Yuezhi; Zhang Qian found it in 126 without a political system.

certainty.note: Satrapy and city frontiers (Bactra, Ai-Khanoum, Taxila, the Arius), the Oxus, the Hindu Kush and the Indus plain are approximate; no treaty fixed a line, and the Indian conquests have only a footnote's regions.
